principles: Questions must require the stimulus when one is supplied.
Distractors should represent plausible misconceptions, not jokes or impossible forms.
Visuals must encode information needed to answer, not merely decorate the page.
Higher-difficulty items should combine at least two reasoning steps or sources of evidence.
Explanations must identify the decisive reasoning, not only restate the answer.
Science conclusions must stay within the evidence supplied.
Mathematics items should test interpretation as well as calculation.
English items should include inference, synthesis, vocabulary-in-context and writer craft.
